mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weekly means (-36.0, -33.4, -29.9, -28.3) in lockstep with TRANSIT (-32.9 to -21.0). Because the gap to baseline remains large, the relaxation trend continues and the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC lands above the trailing mean of -31.9.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly mean improved from -36.0 to -28.3 between t-3w and t-0w
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the trailing 28-day mean of -31.9.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen from 10.1 to 8.7, so households are spending measurably less time at home. Each point of lost stay-at-home surplus is converted into out-of-home trips that skew toward discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 9.0 (crossed at t-0w, 8.7)
regime_hint: post-lockdown reopening with falling stay-at-home time
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the two weeks after RESIDENTIAL sits below 9.0 is at or below the last four weekly means observed at the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: Commuting restoration requires WORKPLACES and TRANSIT to move together; over t-3w to t-0w they rose 5.6 and 11.9 points respectively. The joint recovery re-anchors lunchtime and after-work retail demand near offices, compounding into higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves at least 2 points week-on-week and TRANSIT improves at least 3 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES +5.6 and TRANSIT +11.9 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: In weeks where both thresholds are met, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not above the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossed from -2.6 to +3.3 inside three weeks, marking the end of bulk-restocking behaviour and a return to routine errand patterns. Normalised grocery trips are chained with adjacent discretionary stops, so RETAIL_REC gains follow within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean crosses above 0.0 (crossed at t-1w, +2.0)
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -4.6 at t-3w to +3.3 at t-0w
regime_hint: reopening with grocery normalisation above baseline
failure_condition: In the week following a GROCERY_PHARM reading above 0.0, RETAIL_REC is at or below the trailing four-week mean of -31.9.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS is still the deepest deficit at -35.6 even after a 5.3-point four-week recovery, so outdoor leisure demand is only partially restored. As the outdoor season advances, the spending pool parks represent rotates into retail-and-recreation, raising the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -40.9 to -35.6 but remains the most depressed category
regime_hint: spring-to-summer outdoor season under easing restrictions
failure_condition: PARKS continues to improve week-on-week while the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean stays at or below -31.9.

mechanism_narrative: An 11.9-point four-week TRANSIT gain signals contact rates rising fast enough to seed renewed transmission. Authorities respond with capacity limits or partial closures within roughly three weeks, capping retail footfall so the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean falls below the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: cumulative four-week TRANSIT gain reaches at least 10 points (observed +11.9)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -32.9 at t-3w to -21.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: accelerating reopening immediately before restriction re-imposition
failure_condition: After a TRANSIT four-week gain of 10 points or more, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean remains above the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Falling RESIDENTIAL (10.1 to 8.7) combined with rising WORKPLACES (-38.7 to -33.1) is the joint signature of households leaving home for work again. The resulting daytime co-presence generates after-work retail trips that raise RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL down 1.4 points and WORKPLACES up 5.6 points across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Weeks showing falling RESIDENTIAL together with rising WORKPLACES are followed by RETAIL_REC at or below its trailing four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM rising to +3.3 above baseline flags renewed precautionary stockpiling of essentials rather than full normalisation. Households redirect trip budgets to bulk essentials, draining discretionary retail visits so RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks stays at or below the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean exceeds +3.0 (reached at t-0w, +3.3)
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at +3.3 while RETAIL_REC remains 28.3 points below baseline
regime_hint: reopening with renewed precautionary essential-goods demand
failure_condition: In the two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +3.0, RETAIL_REC is above the trailing four-week mean of -31.9.
